dimension_1_problem_framing.text: The paper addresses the problem of estimating the fill probability (execution likelihood) of RFQ responses in institutional algorithmic trading of European corporate bonds, treating accurate fill probability estimation as a core and competitively important component of market-making strategies. It formulates the study as finding quantum data transformations that reduce prediction error for fill-probability models over confined intraday trading periods, using market-state representations built from RFQ and surrounding market information.

dimension_2_quantum_method.text: The approach uses a Projected Quantum Feature Map (PQFM) as the quantum transformation, implemented via gate-based circuits on IBM Heron/ibm_torino hardware and noiseless simulators, to generate enriched feature vectors from market-state inputs. Quantum-generated features are produced offline as a decoupled component, measured to yield classical quantities that can be stored and reused, and are integrated into downstream classical statistical learning models for fill probability estimation.

dimension_3_key_results.text: Using real production-scale intraday RFQ data, the authors report a relative out-of-sample performance gain of up to 34% in trade backtesting scores for models that use quantum hardware–transformed features compared with those that do not. These uplifts are observed when models are trained on datasets where the inputs have been transformed by quantum algorithms executed on IBM Heron/ibm_torino devices, with the headline result being an overall performance gain of up to 34% across models.

dimension_4_classical_comparison.text: The study compares models with and without access to quantum hardware–transformed data, showing that classical statistical learning models augmented with quantum features can achieve higher out-of-sample test scores than their purely classical counterparts, with reported uplifts of up to 34%. This comparison is structured around identical downstream model classes, differing only in whether they consume the original classical feature set or the quantum-transformed features.

dimension_5_stated_limitations.text: The authors emphasize that they do not infer any generalizable theory or causal economic mechanism from the observed performance gains, stressing that the analysis is empirical and dataset-specific without generalization guarantees. They acknowledge that inherent noise in current quantum hardware appears to contribute to the observed uplift, but the exact role of this intrinsic noise in driving performance gains is not understood, especially given observed noise-induced drifts across repeated hardware runs. Consequently, the specific quantum feature map cannot be used to claim a theoretical explanation of the effects, and attempts to reproduce the hardware benefits with artificially induced noise in simulations fail, underscoring that the results remain heuristic and not theoretically grounded.

dimension_6_future_work.text: The paper notes that clarifying the exact role of intrinsic quantum hardware noise in producing the observed performance gains requires further investigation, indicating that future work should focus on disentangling noise effects and developing a theoretical understanding of why certain noisy hardware executions appear empirically beneficial.

dimension_7_novelty_claim.text: The contribution lies in proposing and empirically testing a hybrid architecture in which projected quantum feature maps, generated on real quantum hardware from realistic corporate bond RFQ market states, are integrated as an offline, decoupled feature-generation component to enhance fill probability models. Within this realistic market-making setting and large-scale intraday dataset, the authors present empirical evidence that hardware-generated quantum features can yield substantial performance uplifts, while explicitly refraining from claiming a general quantum advantage or theoretical explanation.

dimension_8_methodological_notes.text: Methodologically, the study uses a large, proprietary, production-scale intraday dataset of European corporate bond RFQs, filtering to an active window and non-maturing bonds to obtain a substantial labeled sample of 143,912 RFQs and constructing high-dimensional market-state feature vectors that capture micro- to macro-scale statistical characteristics. The system architecture deliberately decouples quantum feature generation (run offline as PQFM transformations on hardware or simulator) from the online real-time response system, with all quantum outputs reduced to classical feature vectors for storage and downstream use, reflecting a practically motivated hybrid design grounded in real trading data.
